title: What If Every Cloud on Earth Vanished? A 5 Degree Jump

scenes.text: What if every cloud on Earth vanished? The clear blue sky would be the least of it.
Clouds cover roughly two thirds of the planet, and they bounce back 30 to 60 percent of the sunlight that hits them.
From orbit, NOAA measures it: clouds reflect about 50 watts per square meter, but trap 30 back as heat.
That nets out to about 20 watts of cooling on every square meter of the planet.
Take them away and Earth absorbs nearly 20 percent more solar heat. The surface ends up roughly 5 degrees Celsius warmer.
Clouds look like decoration. They are a thermostat, quietly holding the whole planet cooler than it would be.
